title: Security tight as biker appears in court
article: Fearing retribution from motorcycle gang rivals, machine-gun toting tactical officers patrolled inside and outside the downtown courthouse as an alleged biker gang member, implicated in the wounding of an Ontario Provincial Police officer last month, appeared briefly in court yesterday.

Marc Bouffard, whose lawyer readily admits he was a member of the notorious Rockers, a puppet club for the Hells Angels, sported a bulletproof vest as he was led shackled and handcuffed into the courtroom in the company of five members of the OPP's Tactical Unit.

Wearing glasses and sporting a goatee, Mr. Bouffard, 27, stood throughout the proceeding and bit his lip as he peered throughout the courtroom, virtually empty except for his escort, investigators and reporters.

At one point, Mr. Bouffard asked the justice of the peace why he would not be attending his next court date. He was told it would be done by video from his new home, the maximum security wing at the Ottawa-Carleton Regional Detention Centre.
In minutes, his appearance was over and April 19 was set as a date for a judicial pre-trial and a remand scheduled for April 22.
Mr. Bouffard was driving along Highway 401 with career criminal Daniel Lamer the morning of March 10 when an OPP officer, believing they were speeding, stopped their car near Morrisburg.

While Mr. Bouffard was being questioned in an OPP cruiser, a gunfight erupted between Mr. Lamer and several OPP officers. In the ensuing exchange, Mr. Lamer was shot dead and Const. Dan Brisson suffered a minor wound to his neck.

Mr. Bouffard was originally charged with obstructing police, mischief and impersonation, but those three charges were rolled into new set of charges, which now number 16. The new slate includes one count of attempted murder, 11 weapons-related offences, including possession of a prohibited weapon and breach of probation.

"What has to be made clear is that Mr. Bouffard was not a member of the Rockers at the time of this incident," said Montreal lawyer Gilbert Frigon, who has previously represented Mr. Bouffard. "He was a member at other times, but not when this happened.
"I have never heard of his associate. I do not know who he was."
The only thing regulars at the courthouse could talk about was the overwhelming police presence in and around the very modern facility.
Two tactical officers blocked the door to courtroom No. 1 as a Cornwall police officer searched everyone entering the courtroom for Mr. Bouffard's appearance.
Several other tactical officers and other uniformed police officers patrolled the parking lot while at least 10 plainclothes officers milled about the lobby awaiting the appearance.

Shortly after 1:30 p.m., heavily armed tactical officers took up positions at several locations in the rear parking lot of the courthouse, facing Third Street West. Minutes later, an unmarked cruiser with Mr. Bouffard in the rear seat, raced from a courthouse parking garage onto the street, where several other police vehicles joined in a motorcade to escort Mr. Bouffard to Ottawa.
The OPP investigation into the shooting is ongoing as detectives try to determine where the heavily armed pair were heading when they were stopped.

There's also the independent investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit, which has centred on one of three officers at the scene as the officer responsible for the shooting of Mr. Lamer.
